prior_importants.description: committedFixRound ignores a steer after the round's session_done, so a steered session gets 'fix committed Nm ago, awaiting re-gate / pup merge <id> --pr' while its worker is still working, even with the conductor running.

findings.description: The test comment "A steer hands the worker more to do and leaves it awaiting-review" repeats the committedFixRound JSDoc, and the `it` title already states the behaviour, so the comment can go.

refuted_findings.description: When a steer follows a fix round's `session_done` and the worker's reply turn ends without a new `pup session done`, `fixCommitted` stays undefined for good. While the conductor runs, `needOf` then gives the session no line at all, and the merge lock sits idle with nothing pointing at it.
refuted_findings.refutation: This is the intended design, not a regression. ADR 0102 deliberately keeps an awaiting-review session out of the inbox while the conductor runs; the session stays in `pup status`, the table and the web dashboard's awaiting-review group. The existing refused-gate exception follows the same rule: `newestGateRefused` (dashboard.service.ts:1101) treats a steer and a new session_done alike, and the test 'is the conductor's again after a steer' expects an empty inbox. The delta applies that rule to the fix-committed line, which was the point of the prior-round finding, and the new test pins this behaviour on purpose.
